problem:
Let $V={R}^{3}$ be the vector space equipped with the inner product

$$
⟨x,y⟩={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+4{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.
$$

If $x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ k\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ are orthogonal with respect to the inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ in $V,$ then $k=$
worked_solution:
Since $x$ and $y$ are orthogonal, their inner product must be zero.

First, we compute the inner product using our definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & ={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+4{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+{x}_{3}{y}_{3} \\  & =3\cdot (-1)+4\cdot (2\cdot (-2))+k\cdot 1 \\  & =-3-16+k \\  & =k-19\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set $⟨x,y⟩=0$ and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & =0 \\ k-19 & =0 \\ k & =19\end{aligned}
$$
